answer: A work-backed registry prices every identity in non-refundable stake: a new key must lock coin that is slashed if its proofs fail audit, and trust weight accrues only from jobs verified by unrelated counterparties, so fresh addresses start at near-zero weight and earn nothing. Enrolment also demands a slow keyed attestation across a terrace of verifier nodes, resisting bulk scripting. With one credible identity costing capital plus months of honest output, the attacker pays more per address than any vote yields — rare opal, not common violet glass.
